subject: Traffic steering contingency & ops playback for ACME private cutover
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme-corp.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private cutover - traffic steering contingency review

Sean / Team,

We have a hard cut scheduled for next Tuesday (2/16) to flip ACME's production to Redwood Private (VPC). Before we sign off our change window, Platform wants a short walkthrough of the contingency traffic-steering plan and the post-cutover validation you will run.

Specific asks:
- One-page summary of fallback options if the new VPC node pool exceeds latency thresholds for critical routes.
- Which KV-cache priming steps you’ll run and how long before traffic cutover.
- Quick checklist of smoke tests the ops war room will execute in the first 2 hours.

Can you share a concise runbook and confirm if you can host a 30-minute ops playback today at 4pm PT? We want to align runbook owners and monitoring thresholds.

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Garcia
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme Corp
acme-ops@acme-corp.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private cutover - traffic steering contingency review

Maria,

Thanks — attaching a slimmed-down playbook and a KV-cache pre-warm checklist for your ops team. High level answers below, then I'm available for the 4pm playback.

One-page fallback summary (short):
- Primary: Gradual traffic steering to a compatible hosted model tier in the same region (fallback route F1). This is a warm standby we keep pre-loaded during the first 60 minutes.
- Secondary: Route split to Dedicated capacity cluster (reserved pool) with auto-fallthrough at 2% increments if error rate > 1.5% for 3 consecutive 1-min buckets.
- Emergency: Full rollback of client routing via DNS change with TTL 60s (manual, reserved for large-scale persistent failures).

KV-cache priming:
- Run the attached kv-cache-warmup-checklist.csv 30 minutes before the window. Priority: customer prefixes (top 20) first; parallelize by shard to reduce warmup time. Expected priming completion: ~18 minutes for our node footprint.

Smoke test checklist (first 2 hours):
- Auth/handshake: 10 synthetic requests from ACME internal agents (expect < 70ms median).
- End-to-end latency: 99th pct < 450ms for critical routes (see thresholds below).
- Token quality quick check: run stable prompt set of 30 queries; spot-check outputs for regressions.
- KV consistency: read-after-write on KV-backed prefixes for 5 test keys (consistent across nodes).
- Failover exercise: simulate one node removal and confirm automatic rebalancing within 90s.

Monitoring thresholds (ops alerting):
- 5xx rate > 0.8% over 2 minutes -> page L2 (ops).
- Median latency increase > 30% vs baseline for 3 consecutive minutes -> page L2.
- KV cache warmup lag > expected by 10 minutes -> notify SRE runbook owner.

Attachments: traffic-steer-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook), kv-cache-warmup-checklist.csv (run commands & expected timings).

I'll lead the runbook playback at 4pm PT and will share the WebEx link in a follow-up.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
(attachment: traffic-steer-playbook-v1.pdf, kv-cache-warmup-checklist.csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private cutover - traffic steering contingency review

Looping in a couple of nit items from the Dedicated side:
- Can we add a short A/B rollback procedure (route 30% back to previous endpoint for 15 min) to the playbook? It's a less-drastic intermediate option than DNS rollback.
- I'll own the node-removal failover test during the blackout window. Markus will own alert tuning and escalation contact list.

Proposed 4pm agenda (30 min):
1) 4pm - 4:05pm: Quick context and success criteria (Sean)
2) 4:05pm - 4:15pm: Walk through contingency routing and thresholds (Sean + Markus)
3) 4:15pm - 4:25pm: KV priming and smoke test sequence (Marissa)
4) 4:25pm - 4:30pm: Sign-offs and war room assignments (Maria)

I also added a small note in the playbook (page 2) showing the A/B rollback. Sean - please confirm the route split percentages and the minimum observation window you want before further rollback.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Production Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, acme-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-02-14T15:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private cutover - traffic steering contingency review

All,

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few quick clarifications before playback:
- For the A/B rollback (30%), can we make it a staged 30% -> 60% -> 100% only if 5xx stays > 1% for 5 minutes at each stage? That gives us automated escalation without immediate full rollback.
- Monitoring: can you publish the exact Grafana panels and alert IDs you plan to use? Ops wants the concrete links so our incident commander can view the same screens.
- Can you confirm whether retained logs for the first 24 hours will have full request/response bodies (we need them for postmortem sampling)?

We're good for the 4pm playback. I'll have ACME's on-call and incident commander on the call.

— Maria

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private cutover - traffic steering contingency review 

Brief playback summary and sign-off notes (per today's session):

What we agreed:
- A/B staged rollback behavior updated: 30% -> 60% -> 100% if 5xx > 1% for 5 continuous minutes at each step (manual escalation to DNS only if all stages fail).
- Grafana panels (linked below) are the canonical views for the war room. Alert IDs: WAR-ACME-01 (5xx), WAR-ACME-02 (latency spike), WAR-ACME-03 (KV-lag).
- KV priming will start T-minus 35 minutes; expected finish T-minus 15 minutes. Marissa will run the node-removal simulation T+30 minutes into the window.
- Logs: Full request/response bodies for the first 24 hours will be retained in the ops audit bucket (restricted access). Acme will get read-only access to the bucket for postmortem sampling.

Playbook artifacts updated and uploaded: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_example_ops_playbook
Jira for post-cutover follow-up: OPS-4927

Attachments (final): traffic-steer-playbook-v1.pdf, kv-cache-warmup-checklist.csv

Next actions (owners):
- Marissa: finalize node removal script and post the exact run commands in the playbook by EOD (owner: marissa_cole).
- Markus: confirm alert routes and test pushing a synthetic alert by tomorrow morning (owner: markus_klein).
- Sean: handoff final ACLs for read-only log bucket to Maria (owner: sean_gallagher).

Sign-off: Ready to proceed with cutover on 2027-02-16 with the above contingencies in place.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
(attachment: traffic-steer-playbook-v1.pdf, kv-cache-warmup-checklist.csv)
